Regional Government

2.1.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, Pasal 19 (BAB VI KERJASAMA) explicitly establishes an inter-institutional cooperation/coordination mechanism: “dapat dilakukan kerja sama dengan” a long list of institutions (perangkat daerah lain, TNI/Polri, kejaksaan, pengadilan, dunia usaha, LSM, pemerintah kabupaten/kota lain, media, etc.) and requires it be formalized: “dituangkan dalam bentuk perjanjian kerjasama” (Art. 19(2)). That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. 6.2.rationale: The original regulation defines “Korban” as “perempuan dan anak” (Pasal 1 angka 7) and defines “Perdagangan Perempuan dan Anak” (Pasal 1 angka 10). It also prohibits trafficking of “perempuan dan anak” (Pasal 23 huruf g: “penculikan, penjualan dan/atau perdagangan perempuan dan anak”). Most importantly, the victim service framework in Pasal 10 is for “Korban” generally (which includes women), including complaint/referral, security protection, psychosocial/psychological rehabilitation, legal assistance, spiritual assistance, safe house, and reintegration. Although Pasal 16 provides special protection explicitly for child trafficking victims, women trafficking victims are still covered as “Korban” under Pasal 10 services and the trafficking prohibition. The judge’s ‘No’ relied on an overly narrow requirement of explicit ‘special protection’ for women trafficking victims; the golden ‘Yes’ is defensible from the Indonesian text because trafficking victims (women included) fall under the protected victim category and receive services. Therefore the discrepancy is best explained by the golden label being correct and the judge being too strict; however since the judge only had the same passages and still could have concluded Yes from Pasal 1(7), Pasal 1(10), Pasal 10, and Pasal 23(g), this points to the golden label not being wrong. (If your coding scheme requires an explicit targeted measure for women trafficking victims beyond general victim services, then the golden label would be questionable—but the text supports inclusion of women trafficking victims via the general victim-services provisions.)

6.10.rationale: Pasal 13 provides “Perlindungan Khusus” for children in emergency situations, including “pengungsi anak” (child refugees), and specifies handling and basic services (including without regard to citizenship status). The indicator, however, is “Refugees / displacement” under an intersectional approach; the golden label ‘No’ suggests the coding expects measures for refugees/displaced persons generally (or at least women survivors), not only children. The judge marked ‘Yes’ based solely on child-refugee provisions, which is an over-broad interpretation if the indicator is meant to cover refugees/displacement as a group beyond children. The evidence supports child refugees only, so the judge’s reasoning likely caused the false positive.
